paper.title: Structure-aware graph neural network based deep transfer learning framework for enhanced predictive analytics on diverse materials datasets
paper.research_summary: This paper presents a structure-aware graph neural network (GNN) based deep transfer learning framework to improve predictive performance for materials properties when training data is sparse. It leverages the ALIGNN architecture trained on large source datasets (e.g., Materials Project formation energy) and transfers knowledge via fine-tuning or feature extraction to build target models on smaller, diverse datasets (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental). Evaluation across 115 dataset-property combinations shows transfer learning outperforms scratch-trained models in ≈90% of cases, with particular gains for small datasets and extrapolation tasks.

tasks.objective: to accurately predict materials properties prior to synthesis to prioritize resources for simulations and experiments
constraints: costly and time-consuming experiments and DFT computations
input_requirements: structure files (e.g., atomic positions for POSCAR)
output_goal: reliable and accurate predictive models for materials properties

evidence.text: An essential component in the process of materials discovery is to know which material(s) will possess desirable properties. For many materials properties, performing experiments and density functional theory computations are costly and time-consuming. Hence, it is challenging to build accurate predictive models for such properties using conventional data mining methods due to the small amount of available data.

Accurate materials property prediction using crystal structure occupies a primary and often critical role in materials science, particularly when screening through a near-infinite space of candidate materials for desirable materials performance.

Here we present a framework for materials property prediction tasks using structure information that leverages graph neural network-based architecture along with deep-transfer-learning techniques to drastically improve the model’s predictive ability on diverse materials (3D/2D, inorganic/organic, computational/experimental) data.

stage_output: source dataset (e.g., Materials Project formation energy)
target datasets (e.g., JARVIS-3D, JARVIS-2D, Flla, DC, PT, EFE, KEFE, KEB, HOPV)

evidence.text: We use nine datasets of DFT-computed and experimental properties in this work: Materials Project (MP)4, Joint Automated Repository for Various Integrated Simulations (JARVIS) 3D with 46 properties and 2D with 32 properties5, Flla44 with three properties, Dielectric Constant (DC)45 with five properties, Piezoelectric Tensor (PT)46 with two properties, Experimental Formation Energy (EFE)47 with one property, Kingsbury Experimental Formation Energy (KEFE)48 with one property, Kingsbury Experimental Bandgap (KEB)49 with one property, and Harvard Organic Photovoltaic Dataset (HOPV)50 with 24 properties.

MP dataset was downloaded from39, JARVIS-3D (https://figshare.com/collections/ALIGNN_data/5429274), JARVIS-2D (https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/26808917) and HOPV (https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/28814184) from their respective figshare links and the rest of the datasets were obtained using Matminer51.

stages.stage_name_raw: training of source model on large dataset
stages.stage_goal: to train a structure-aware GNN (ALIGNN) on a large source dataset to learn generalizable representations

evidence.text: A model trained on the formation energy of the MP dataset39 is used as the source model to perform fine-tuning and feature extraction-based transfer learning as formation energy has shown to lead to meaningful representations from large source datasets36, which can then be applied during the model training on the smaller target datasets to improve their predictive performance.

We use a structure-aware GNN-based architecture, ALIGNN39 as our base architecture for training the source models, performing transfer learning using fine-tuning method, and extracting structure-based features, as it has shown to significantly outperform other known GNN models31,40–42,52 for materials property prediction across a wide variety of datasets with different data sizes39 using crystal structure information as the model input.

stages.stage_goal: to generate target models using transfer learning techniques (fine-tuning and feature extraction) on small target datasets

evidence.text: The transfer of information can be performed by either fine-tuning or feature extraction methods. Fine-tuning uses the weights from the pre-trained model as the preliminary weight initialization for the network, which are further refined using the target dataset. In the feature extraction method, we treat the pre-trained model as a feature extractor to extract robust features for the target dataset and use them to build the target model using representation learning.

For TL models, we use a model pretrained on the MP dataset with formation energy as the materials property using ALIGNN as the model architecture. The TL techniques comprise of traditional fine-tuning and a feature extraction method from a graph neural network.

stages.stage_goal: to compare the predictive accuracy of transfer learning models against scratch-trained models using mean absolute error (MAE)

evidence.text: We compare models obtained using the proposed framework with models trained from scratch (SC).
We use mean absolute error (MAE) as the primary evaluation metric for all models.
Table 2 presents the prediction accuracy of the best SC and best TL model on the test set for each of the 48 target properties.
